summary: This is a JUnit test class for the TrafficLight class, checking each colour in the cycle and whether the light requires drivers to stop. Each test creates a fresh light, advances it as far as needed, and then asserts one thing about the result.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is what marks a method as a test the framework should run.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping the tests short and readable.
The convention is to name the test class after the class under test with Test appended, so this file clearly belongs to TrafficLight.
Test names read as sentences describing the expected behaviour, so a failure report tells you what the code got wrong.
Each test builds its own light, so no test can be affected by changes another test made.
Checks the starting state: the expected value comes first and the actual value second.
assertTrue passes only when the method returns true, which is what a red light should demand.
Calling advance once moves the light one step through its cycle, which is the action this test is examining.
Confirms the first transition in the cycle takes red to green.
assertFalse is the mirror of assertTrue and documents that a green light lets traffic through.
Two advance calls are needed to reach yellow; the setup calls come before the blank line and the action being tested after it.
Verifies the second transition, from green to yellow.
Three advances bring the light back to its starting colour, proving the sequence loops rather than getting stuck.
Yellow also requires stopping, so this test pins down a rule that is easy to break when someone edits isStopRequired.
